The present petition filed under Section 482 Cr.P.C. seeks quashing of FIR No. 259/2015, under Sections 420/120-B IPC, registered at P.S. Lodhi Colony, Delhi.

2. Learned counsel appearing on behalf of the petitioners submits that during the pendency of the investigation in the aforesaid FIR , the latter have entered into separate MoUs with respondent no. 2 to 8 and have settled their dispute.

3. The status report dated 06.05.2024 authored by Insp. Sanjeev Mandal, SHO/Lodhi Colony with regard to the same has been handed up in Court and the same is taken on record wherein it has been recorded as under:-

sentences.text: In this regard it is submitted that during investigation, complainants were telephonically contacted regarding to verify the factum of settlement between the parties in the above said matter.

On 04.05.2024, the complainants namely (1) S.M.
Srivastava (2) Ashish Agrawal (3) Vinod Kumar (4) Kishore Kumar Kaul (5) Daya Prakash & (6) Rajdeep Agrawal filed their written statement wherein they stated that they all had already settled their dispute with the accused company M/s Celebration Hotel & Resorts Pvt. Ltd. & Ors. and the settlement documents have been executed with the accused persons.
They have no objection if the FIR No. 259/2015 U/s 420/120B IPC PS Lodhi Colony, is quashed by the Hon'ble High Court.
They do not want to any further action on the above said case.

(Copy of statements enclosed for kind perusal along with self-attested copies of their ID's).
3.

One of the complainants namely Mr. Ashish Agrawal also filed a separate written statement wherein it is stated that he is travelling to U.S.A from 8th May 2024 to 215 May 2024 and unable to attend the Hon'ble Court through V.C due to time zone difference.
He requested for exemption of personal appearance before the Hon'ble Court.

(Copy of written statement enclosed for kind perusal)."
4.

Petitioners are present before the Court and respondent no.2,3,5,6,7 and 8 are present through video conferencing and have been duly identified by the Investigating Officer, SI Shiv Singh, P.S.
Lodhi Colony.
5. The respondent No.2,3,5,6,7,8 states that the matter has been settled with the petitioners as well as other persons named in the FIR and they have no objection if the FIR is quashed.
Respondent no.4 is stated to be in the USA and on an oral request, he has been exempted from personal appearance.
His statement has been recorded by the Investigating Officer.
6. In view of the settlement between the parties, learned APP for the State also has no objection if the present FIR is quashed.
7. In Gian Singh v. State of Punjab, (2012) 10 SCC 303, the Honble Supreme Court has recognized the need of amicable resolution of disputes This is a digitally signed order.

2 end and if the answer to the above question(s) is in the affirmative, the High Court shall be well within its jurisdiction to quash the criminal proceeding."

sentences.text:
8. In view of the aforesaid circumstances, and the fact that the parties have put a quietus to the dispute, no useful purpose will be served in continuing with the present FIR No. 259/2015, under Sections 420/120-B IPC, registered at P.S. Lodhi Colony, Delhi..
9.
In the interest of justice, the petition is allowed, and the FIR No. 259/2015, under Sections 420/120-B IPC, registered at P.S. Lodhi Colony, Delhi, is hereby quashed.
10. Petition is allowed and disposed of accordingly.
11. Pending application(s), if any, also stand disposed of.
AMIT SHARMA, J MAY 14, 2024/nk
